messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Spanish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Spanish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Spanish) | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------| | Ed | discourse marker “And” | **Y** | “and” | OK | | ecco | exclamatory pointer “lo!” | **he aquí** | “here is / lo!” | OK | | quasi | adverb “almost” | **casi** | “almost” | OK | | al | preposition + definite article “at the” | **al** | “at the” | OK | | cominciar | noun “beginning” | **comienzo** | “beginning” | OK | | de | preposition “of” | **de** | “of” | OK | | l'erta | noun “the steep (path)” | **la cuesta** | “the steep (road)” | OK | | una | indefinite article “a” | **una** | “a” | OK | | lonza | noun “she‑leopard” | **leona** | “she‑leopard / lioness” | OK | | leggera | adjective “light” | **ligera** | “light” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | **y** | “and” | OK | | presta | adjective “nimble” | **ágil** | “nimble / agile” | OK | | molto | adverb “very” | **muy** | “very” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which / that” | **que** | “which / that” | OK | | di | preposition “with” | **de** | “with / of” | OK | | pel | noun “coat / fur” | **pelaje** | “coat / fur” | OK | | macolato | past participle used adjectivally “spotted” | **manchado** | “spotted” | OK | | era | copular verb “was” (imperf.) | **estaba** | “was” (imperfect) | OK | | coverta | past participle (passive) “covered” | **cubierta** | “covered” | OK |
### Items to Note - **MISSING:** none - **WRONG:** none - **GRAMMAR:** none (all gender/number agreements are correct) - **UNNECESSARY:** none (no source elements were omitted or superfluous in the Spanish rendering)
All source tokens are accounted for, correctly translated, and grammatically appropriate in the Spanish version.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Spanish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 31** - Original: Y he aquí, casi al comienzo de la cuesta, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 32** - Original: una leona ligera y muy ágil, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 33** - Original: que de pelaje manchado estaba cubierta; - Issue: word order is awkward in Spanish - Corrected: que estaba cubierta de pelaje manchado;
```text Y he aquí, casi al comienzo de la cuesta, una leona ligera y muy ágil, que estaba cubierta de pelaje manchado; ```
